ideas.pitch: An AI-powered multi-language syntax debugger and logical optimization sandbox designed for competitive programming and code review.
ideas.title: SyntaxSage
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core themes of the event—programming knowledge, logical thinking, and debugging skills—appealing heavily to computer applications faculty judges.

ideas.pitch: A real-time collaborative coding and peer debugging workspace tailored for two-person student teams to tackle multi-level programming challenges.
ideas.title: AlgoDuet
ideas.why_it_could_win: Aligns with the team size of two and the competitive programming structure of Optiquest 2026, offering utility directly during the event setup.

ideas.pitch: An automated MCQ test generator and logic evaluation engine parsing C, Java, and Python syntax to create custom adaptive quizzes.
ideas.title: LogicLoom
ideas.why_it_could_win: Reflects the format of the Prelims round (Technical Proficiency Test covering C, Java, and Python syntax and logic), making it deeply relevant to the department organizers.

ideas.pitch: A visualization tool that steps through complex C, Java, and Python control flows to reveal execution paths and memory states for debugging.
ideas.title: TraceCode
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses debugging skills and problem-solving abilities highlighted in the event description with hard engineering on code AST parsing.

ideas.pitch: A gamified programming challenge hub with integrated automated test case validation across multiple difficulty tiers.
ideas.title: QueryQuest
ideas.why_it_could_win: Matches the multi-level programming challenges format of the competition, providing a polished platform demonstration for judges.
